cards.title: Card types
cards.intro: The deck has 108 cards in four colours. Each colour has its own symbol (flame, sun, leaf and drop), so you never rely on colour alone.
cards.s1b: 0 to 9 in every colour. They are the core of the game and score their number.
cards.s2b: Skip, Reverse and Draw Two have a colour and change the pace of the game.
cards.s3b: Wild and Wild Draw Four have no colour: when you play one you choose the next colour.

turns.title: Turns and direction
turns.summary: What you can play and when to draw
turns.intro: Everyone starts with 7 cards. On your turn you play a card that matches the one on the table.
turns.s1b: A card of the same colour, the same number or the same symbol. Wilds can be played almost any time.
turns.s2b: Draw one card. If it fits you may play it; otherwise you pass.
turns.s3b: Play goes clockwise. Reverse flips it; with two players it works like a Skip.

specials.title: Special cards
specials.intro: Special cards are your best tool to slow down whoever is winning.
specials.s1b: Skip: the next player loses their turn. Reverse: play changes direction.
specials.s2b: The next player draws 2 cards and loses their turn.
specials.s3b: You choose the new colour. With +4 the next player also draws 4 and loses their turn; you may only play it when you have no card of the current colour.

uno.title: Calling UNO
uno.summary: Warn everyone when you have one card left
uno.intro: When you are about to be down to a single card you have to warn the others.
uno.s1b: Tap “UNO!” as you play your second-to-last card.
uno.s2b: If you are left with one card without calling it and a rival catches you, you draw 2 penalty cards.
uno.s3b: If a rival forgot to call UNO, tap the alert to make them draw. Drawing a card cancels UNO.

strategy.title: Strategy and scoring
strategy.summary: Tips and how a game is won
strategy.intro: The first player out of cards wins the round and scores the cards left in the rivals' hands.
strategy.s1b: Numbers score their value, action cards 20 and wilds 50. The first to 500 points wins the game.
strategy.s2b: Save them for the end or to stop someone about to win. Switch to the colour you hold most of.
strategy.s3b: Keep an eye on how many cards they have and use Draw Two or Skip on whoever is closest to winning.

blackjack.title: Blackjack
blackjack.intro: You play against the dealer. Whoever gets closer to 21 without going over wins.
blackjack.s1b: 2 to 10 count their number, face cards 10 and an Ace 1 or 11. An Ace plus a ten-value card as your first two is Blackjack.
blackjack.s2b: Hit: take a card. Stand: keep your hand. Double: double the bet and take exactly one card. Split: turn a pair into two hands.
blackjack.s3b: The dealer draws to 17 and stands. A win pays 1 to 1, Blackjack 3 to 2 and a push returns your bet.

roulette.title: Roulette
roulette.summary: Bet on numbers, colours or dozens
roulette.intro: Single-zero European roulette. Pick a chip, place it on the layout and spin.
roulette.s1b: Pick the chip value below and tap spots. Each tap adds one chip; you can undo or clear before spinning.
roulette.s2b: Straight up (one number) pays 35 to 1. Dozens and columns 2 to 1. Red, black, even, odd and halves 1 to 1.
roulette.s3b: If 0 comes up every outside bet loses. Only a bet on 0 wins.

slots.title: Slots
slots.intro: Gold Rush has 5 reels and up to 10 paylines. Win with 3, 4 or 5 matching symbols from the left.
slots.s1b: Choose 1, 5 or 10 lines and the bet per line. Your total bet is lines × bet per line.
slots.s2b: The sheriff star stands in for any symbol and also pays on its own.
slots.s3b: Five sevens on a line is the jackpot. Help shows the full paytable and every line.

fair.title: Provably fair
fair.how: Before any bet, the server fixes this round's secret seed and shows its SHA-256 fingerprint. Every card or pocket comes from that seed (HMAC-SHA256). When the round ends the seed is revealed: if its SHA-256 matches the fingerprint and it gives the same result, nobody could change the outcome after seeing the bets.

fair.none: The seed is revealed when the first round ends.

rules.r1: 5 reels, 3 rows and {lines} paylines, always active. Your bet is split across all lines.

rules.fairLocal: This version has no server: every round is decided on your device with the browser's cryptographic generator and this machine's math, charged and paid in one step, never twice. Because it all happens on your device it is not tamper-proof: once the game server is connected, results and balance are decided there.
rules.fairRemote: Every round is decided by the server with this machine's math: it checks your balance, books the bet, draws the reels, free spins and bonus, computes the payout and updates your balance before answering. The screen only replays what it receives. A retry never charges or pays twice.

rules.intro: Double-six dominoes (28 tiles), draw variant; with four players there is no boneyard and it plays as a block game, as at Latin tables.
rules.setup:
Everyone gets 7 tiles; the rest is the boneyard (14 with 2 players, 7 with 3, none with 4).
The first hand is opened by whoever holds the highest double (6-6 if it was dealt), who must lead it; if nobody holds a double, the highest tile opens.
Later hands are opened by the previous hand's winner, with any tile. After a blocked hand with no winner the highest double opens again.
rules.turn:
Play in order. Lay a tile that matches one of the two open ends.
With no play, draw from the boneyard one tile at a time until you can play (it stays your turn).
With no play and an empty boneyard, pass.
You may not draw or pass while a tile of yours fits.
rules.end:
Domino: whoever plays their last tile wins the hand.
Blocked: if nobody can play or draw, the lowest hand wins; a tie for lowest means nobody wins the hand.
rules.score:
The hand's winner scores all the pips left in the other hands.
First to the target (100 or 200) wins the match. Two players reaching it with the same score is a tie.

rules.card:
Columns B (1–15), I (16–30), N (31–45), G (46–60) and O (61–75), five different numbers per column.
The centre is FREE and already counts as daubed.
You get a new card every round.
rules.play:
The caller draws balls one at a time, never repeating.
You may only daub numbers on your card that have been called.
rules.win:
A complete line: any row, column or either diagonal.
Press BINGO! when you have one. Calling without a line stops you calling again until 3 more balls are out.
The first valid bingo stops the caller; anyone else holding a line may call it right then and the prize is shared.
rules.score:
Each round gives 100 points to its winners, split evenly.
If all 75 balls go out and nobody calls, the round ends with no winner.
